language: Python; convert every source R example and explain any conversion obstacle

chapters.title: Data, prediction, and correlation
results: Separate quantitative counts, quantitative continuous measurements, and categorical labels; separate cross-sectional, temporal, and panel observations.
For finite-variance nonconstant real random variables, correlation is covariance divided by the product of standard deviations and lies in [-1,1] by Cauchy-Schwarz.
chapters.lab: Typed features, correlation, scaling, and a nonlinear zero-correlation counterexample.

chapters.title: Principal components: variance, geometry, and reconstruction
results: For centered Z and sample covariance S=Z^T Z/(n-1), a unit vector maximizing v^T S v is a leading eigenvector of S.

For an orthogonal rank-k projection onto leading covariance eigenvectors, squared reconstruction error equals (n-1) times the sum of discarded eigenvalues; tied eigenvalues need subspace rather than signed-vector comparisons.
chapters.lab: Covariance versus correlation PCA, SVD, explained variance, reconstruction, and Python conversion of source R demonstrations.

chapters.title: Factor analysis and the limits of latent explanations
results: In x=mu+Lambda f+u with Cov(f)=I, Cov(u)=Psi and Cov(f,u)=0, Cov(x)=Lambda Lambda^T+Psi.
For orthogonal Q, Lambda Q and Q^T f preserve the common-factor covariance; factor orientation is not identified by covariance alone.
chapters.lab: Factor extraction, rotation, communalities and factor-score conventions; inventory and convert all R calls.

chapters.title: Clustering and hierarchical linkage
results: A partition assigns each observation to exactly one nonempty cluster; its usefulness depends on scaling, dissimilarity and the application.
Single, complete and average linkage define between-cluster dissimilarity respectively by the minimum, maximum and mean pairwise dissimilarities.
chapters.lab: Hand-trace agglomeration and compare linkage rules on the same scaled observations.

chapters.title: Ward clustering, dendrograms, and reproducible implementations
results: For Euclidean observations, merging clusters A and B increases within-cluster squared error by |A||B|/(|A|+|B|) times squared centroid distance.
A dendrogram cut defines a partition; display leaf order, tie handling and reported linkage heights depend on conventions and must be audited separately from partition agreement.
chapters.lab: Translate R hierarchical-clustering examples with explicit Ward conventions, distances, labels and cut levels.

chapters.title: K-means as alternating optimization
results: For fixed nonempty assignments, each arithmetic centroid minimizes its cluster's sum of squared Euclidean distances.
Nearest-centroid assignment and centroid recomputation do not increase the k-means objective; this does not guarantee a global minimum.
chapters.lab: Implement Lloyd iterations and compare source initialization/restart conventions with Python.

chapters.title: Simple linear regression: fitting and uncertainty
results: When sum_i(x_i-xbar)^2>0, the intercept-and-slope least-squares minimizer has slope sum_i(x_i-xbar)(y_i-ybar)/sum_i(x_i-xbar)^2 and intercept ybar minus slope times xbar.

Under fixed nonconstant predictors and independent Gaussian errors with common variance, the standardized slope estimator using residual variance with n-2 degrees of freedom has a t distribution for n>2.
chapters.lab: Fit a simple model, derive the output, and distinguish mean-response from new-observation intervals.

chapters.title: Multiple regression and projection geometry
results: For full-column-rank X, the unique least-squares coefficient solves X^T X beta_hat=X^T y, and the residual is orthogonal to col(X).
Under E(epsilon|X)=0 and Cov(epsilon|X)=sigma^2 I, beta_hat is conditionally unbiased with covariance sigma^2 (X^T X)^-1; Gaussianity is additional for exact normal-theory inference.
chapters.lab: Reproduce multiple-regression examples with QR/SVD-based fits and explicit design matrices.

chapters.title: Outliers, leverage, and influence
results: For a rank-q projection H, 0<=h_ii<=1 and sum_i h_ii=q; a large residual and high leverage measure different features of an observation.
If h_ii<1, deleting row i changes its fitted residual into the leave-one-out prediction error e_i/(1-h_ii).
chapters.lab: Translate source diagnostics and compare residual, leverage, studentization, Cook distance, and refits.

chapters.title: Categorical predictors and interpretable contrasts
results: With an intercept, K group indicators sum to the intercept column and are rank deficient; K-1 treatment indicators identify a baseline parameterization when all groups occur.
Changing a full-rank basis for the same design-column space changes coefficients but preserves fitted values and residuals.
chapters.lab: Convert R formula/factor coding into explicit Python contrasts and verify fitted-value equivalence.

chapters.title: Nonlinear features and interaction effects
results: A model polynomial in an observed predictor can remain linear in its regression coefficients.
For conditional mean beta0+beta1 x+beta2 z+beta3 xz, the partial effect with respect to x is beta1+beta3 z; main effects depend on the chosen reference values.
chapters.lab: Convert R transformations and interactions; compare centered and uncentered equivalent fits.

chapters.title: Autocorrelated errors and dependent observations
results: With full-rank fixed X and conditional mean-zero errors, dependence alone does not bias OLS; covariance is (X^T X)^-1 X^T Omega X (X^T X)^-1.
The Durbin-Watson statistic is sum_{i=2}^n(e_i-e_{i-1})^2 divided by sum_i e_i^2; its calibration depends on the regression and ordering assumptions.
chapters.lab: Audit source dependence tests and simulate the difference between coefficient behavior and invalid iid standard errors.

chapters.title: Normality checks and the assumptions behind inference
results: Normality of errors is not required for OLS's algebraic projection or conditional unbiasedness.

Under Gaussian homoscedastic errors, Cov(e|X)=sigma^2(I-H); regression residuals are generally dependent and have unequal marginal variances, so an iid normality-test interpretation needs qualification.
chapters.lab: Convert source tests and Q-Q diagnostics, record test variants, and compare heavy tails with influential observations.

chapters.title: Multicollinearity, identifiability, and conditioning
results: Exact column dependence destroys unique coefficient identification; near dependence can make coefficients unstable even when fitted values are stable.
With an intercept and full rank, variance of slope j under homoscedastic errors is sigma^2/[Sxx_j(1-R_j^2)], where R_j^2 is the auxiliary regression fit of that predictor on the others.
chapters.lab: Convert source VIF/collinearity diagnostics and inspect singular values, coefficient perturbations and predictions.

chapters.title: Heteroscedasticity and variance-aware regression
results: If Omega is known positive definite, minimizing (y-X beta)^T Omega^-1(y-X beta) gives generalized least squares with covariance (X^T Omega^-1 X)^-1 under conditional mean-zero errors.
OLS covariance with nonconstant error variances uses a sandwich form; a sample residual-based estimate requires explicit large-sample conditions and a named finite-sample correction.
chapters.lab: Translate heteroscedasticity tests, weighted fits and covariance conventions; compare fitted means and uncertainty.

chapters.title: Model selection, evaluation, and an end-to-end case study
results: A fitted prediction procedure includes preprocessing and model selection; held-out performance estimates require evaluating the complete procedure without fitting these steps on the held-out outcomes.
AIC and prediction error answer different questions; selecting on the test set invalidates its intended role as an untouched assessment sample.
chapters.lab: Convert all source case-study and selection examples; add a clearly labeled leakage-safe Python evaluation.

chapters.title: Odds ratios and logistic regression
results: If logit P(Y=1|x)=x^T beta, increasing feature j by one unit with all other design coordinates fixed multiplies the odds by exp(beta_j); it does not generally multiply probability by that amount.
For independent Bernoulli responses the logistic log-likelihood has gradient X^T(y-pi) and Hessian -X^T W X, W_ii=pi_i(1-pi_i); separation may prevent a finite unpenalized maximum.
chapters.lab: Convert source odds/logistic examples, disable unintended penalties, and compare likelihood, uncertainty, calibration and thresholds.

chapters.title: Regression discontinuity and local causal identification
results: For sharp treatment D=1{r>=c}, continuity at c of both conditional potential-outcome means and appropriate support identify the jump in E(Y|r) as the treatment effect at the cutoff.
A fitted jump is not causal without the identification assumptions; local polynomial estimation additionally depends on bandwidth, specification and an appropriate uncertainty calculation.
chapters.lab: Convert any source cutoff example; implement a labeled synthetic sharp-design demonstration with sensitivity checks, without claiming formal robust-bias-corrected inference.
